channel.title: FixMyError.net – Recently Added Errors
channel.description: Newly added developer and infrastructure error fixes on FixMyError.net.

item.title: 402 Payment Required
item.description: Reserved in the original HTTP specification and now used by many SaaS APIs to signal that the account is unpaid, out of credit, or over its plan limit. The response body carries the vendor-specific detail.

item.title: 421 Misdirected Request
item.description: The server received a request for a host it cannot serve on that connection. With HTTP/2 connection coalescing, a browser may reuse one TLS connection for several hostnames covered by the same certificate; if the server is not configured for one of them it answers 421.

item.title: 428 Precondition Required
item.description: The server requires the request to be conditional. It is telling the client to send If-Match or If-Unmodified-Since so that concurrent updates cannot silently overwrite one another (the lost update problem).

item.title: 431 Request Header Fields Too Large
item.description: The combined size of the request headers exceeded the server's limit. In practice this is nearly always cookies: an accumulation of analytics, session and feature-flag cookies on one domain.

item.title: 511 Network Authentication Required
item.description: A captive portal — hotel, airport or corporate guest Wi-Fi — is intercepting traffic and requires sign-in. The response comes from the network, not from the server you addressed.

item.title: Android: Duplicate class found in modules
item.description: Two dependencies bring in the same class, usually because one ships a bundled copy of a library that another declares normally, or because two versions of the same artifact are on the classpath under different coordinates.

item.title: Anthropic API: invalid_request_error on tool_use / tool_result
item.description: Tool calling requires strict message pairing: every assistant tool_use block must be answered by a user message containing a tool_result with the matching tool_use_id, in the immediately following turn.

item.title: AWS Bedrock: AccessDeniedException — you don't have access to the model
item.description: Bedrock foundation models must be explicitly enabled per account and per region before they can be invoked, in addition to the usual IAM permissions.

item.title: AWS Lambda: Runtime exited with error: signal: killed
item.description: The function process was killed for exceeding its memory allocation. Lambda reports this rather than an application-level OOM, so the stack trace is absent.

item.title: AWS Lambda: Runtime.ImportModuleError
item.description: The runtime could not load the handler module. Either the handler string does not match the file and export, a dependency is missing from the package, or a native module was built for the wrong architecture or OS.

item.title: AWS S3: SignatureDoesNotMatch
item.description: The SigV4 signature computed by the client differs from the one S3 computed. Causes: wrong secret key, clock skew beyond five minutes, the wrong region in the signing scope, or a proxy that altered headers after signing.

item.title: AWS: AccessDenied when calling the AssumeRole operation
item.description: Role assumption requires permission on both sides: the caller needs sts:AssumeRole in its identity policy, and the target role's trust policy must name the caller as a principal. A denial on either side produces the same message.

item.title: AWS: ExpiredToken / The security token included in the request is expired
item.description: Temporary credentials from STS, IAM Identity Center (SSO) or an assumed role have passed their expiry. Sessions are short-lived by design — one hour by default for an assumed role.

item.title: Azure OpenAI: DeploymentNotFound
item.description: Azure OpenAI addresses a *deployment name* you chose, not the underlying model name. Passing 'gpt-4o' when the deployment is called 'prod-gpt4o' returns 404 DeploymentNotFound.

item.title: Azure: MissingSubscriptionRegistration — resource provider not registered
item.description: Azure requires each resource provider namespace to be registered on the subscription before resources of that type can be created. New subscriptions have only a small default set registered.

item.title: bash: Argument list too long
item.description: A glob expanded to more arguments than the kernel's exec limit allows. The limit is on the total size of arguments plus environment, so a large environment makes it hit sooner.

item.title: bash: bad interpreter: No such file or directory
item.description: The script's shebang line ends with a carriage return, so the kernel looks for an interpreter literally named "/bin/bash\r". The file was saved with Windows line endings, usually via a Git checkout with autocrlf enabled.

item.title: C#: CS8618 non-nullable property must contain a non-null value when exiting constructor
item.description: With nullable reference types enabled, the compiler requires every non-nullable member to be definitely assigned by the end of the constructor. It is warning that the object can be observed in an invalid state.

item.title: C++: runtime error: signed integer overflow (UBSan)
item.description: Signed integer overflow is undefined behaviour in C and C++. The program may appear to work for years and then miscompile after an optimiser change, so UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer reporting it is a real bug, not a false positive.

item.title: cert-manager: Order is pending / challenge failed to propagate
item.description: cert-manager created an ACME order but the challenge never validated. For HTTP-01 the challenge path is not reachable from the internet; for DNS-01 the TXT record has not propagated or the credentials lack permission.

item.title: Cloudflare 520: Web server returns an unknown error
item.description: Cloudflare reached the origin but received a response it could not parse — an empty reply, a connection reset mid-response, oversized headers, or a violation of the HTTP specification.

item.title: Cookie: SameSite=None requires the Secure attribute
item.description: Browsers reject a cookie that declares SameSite=None without Secure. Cross-site cookies must be sent over HTTPS only, so the pair is mandatory. The cookie is silently dropped, which usually shows up as a session that never persists.

item.title: CSP: Refused to execute inline script because it violates the policy
item.description: Content-Security-Policy blocked an inline or an inline event handler. This is the policy preventing the main injection vector for XSS, so the fix is to make the script legitimate rather than to weaken the policy.

item.title: CUDA: driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime version
item.description: The installed NVIDIA driver is older than the CUDA runtime the framework was built against. Drivers are backwards compatible with older runtimes but never forwards compatible with newer ones.

item.title: dbt: Compilation Error — model depends on a node that was not found
item.description: A ref() or source() points at something dbt cannot resolve: a misspelled model name, a source not declared in a .yml file, or a model excluded by the current selector.

item.title: Docker: failed to solve — process did not complete successfully
item.description: A RUN instruction exited non-zero during a BuildKit build. The wrapper message is generic; the real error is in the step output above it, which BuildKit may have collapsed.

item.title: Docker: no matching manifest for linux/arm64
item.description: The image exists but was never published for your CPU architecture. This is routine on Apple Silicon and on ARM cloud instances pulling older images.

item.title: Docker: OCI runtime create failed — executable file not found
item.description: The container was created but runc could not start the entrypoint. The binary named in CMD or ENTRYPOINT does not exist in the image, is not executable, or the script has Windows line endings.

item.title: Expo EAS: build failed — Gradle/Xcode step exited with non-zero code
item.description: EAS Build failed during the native compile step. The wrapper message is generic; the real cause is in the build phase log, and is usually a config plugin conflict, an SDK version mismatch, or a native dependency incompatible with the Expo SDK in use.

item.title: Failed to fetch dynamically imported module
item.description: A single-page app that was loaded before a deployment tried to lazy-load a chunk whose hashed filename no longer exists on the server. The user's open tab is running the previous build.

item.title: Failed to load module script: expected a JavaScript module but got text/html
item.description: The browser requested a .js module and the server returned an HTML page — almost always a 404 handled by an SPA fallback rewriting every unknown path to index.html. The path or base URL is wrong, not the JavaScript.

item.title: Flutter: the current Dart SDK version is X but package requires Y
item.description: A package's environment constraint in pubspec.yaml excludes the Dart SDK bundled with your Flutter version. Dart and Flutter SDK versions are coupled, so the fix is usually to move the Flutter channel rather than the Dart version.

item.title: GCP: SERVICE_DISABLED — API has not been used in project before
item.description: Google Cloud APIs are disabled by default per project. The first call to a service fails until the API is enabled, and there is a short propagation delay after enabling it.

item.title: git: detected dubious ownership in repository
item.description: Git refuses to operate on a repository owned by a different user than the one running git. This safety check blocks a privilege-escalation attack via a malicious repo config, and commonly appears in containers and CI.

item.title: git: refusing to merge unrelated histories
item.description: The two branches have no common ancestor. This normally means a local repository was initialised separately from the remote, or the remote was recreated.

item.title: git: RPC failed; HTTP 400 curl 22 / the remote end hung up unexpectedly
item.description: The push exceeded a size limit somewhere in the chain — the HTTP post buffer, a reverse proxy body limit, or the server's own cap. Large binary files and long histories are the usual triggers.

item.title: GitHub Actions: Failed to save cache — Unable to reserve cache
item.description: Two concurrent jobs tried to save the same cache key, or the repository is at its 10 GB cache limit. Cache save failures are warnings by design and do not fail the build.

item.title: GitHub Actions: this action uses a deprecated Node version
item.description: GitHub retires the Node runtimes that JavaScript actions execute on. An action pinned to an old major continues to run with a warning until the runtime is removed, at which point it fails outright.

item.title: GitHub API: You have exceeded a secondary rate limit
item.description: Separate from the hourly primary quota, GitHub applies secondary limits on burst concurrency, content-creating requests, and expensive queries. They are not exposed in the x-ratelimit headers.

item.title: Go: checksum mismatch — SECURITY ERROR
item.description: The downloaded module's hash does not match go.sum or the public checksum database. This can mean a tampered proxy, but far more often it means an upstream author force-pushed a tag or a private module is being checked against the public sum database.

item.title: Go: missing go.sum entry for module
item.description: A module is required by go.mod but has no checksum recorded in go.sum. Go refuses to build rather than fetching an unverified module — this is the supply-chain check working.

item.title: Go: module requires go >= 1.x (running go 1.y)
item.description: A dependency's go.mod declares a language version newer than your toolchain. Since Go 1.21 the toolchain directive can auto-download a newer Go, but that is disabled in many locked-down CI environments.

item.title: GraphQL: PersistedQueryNotFound
item.description: With automatic persisted queries the client first sends only a hash. If the server has not seen that query before — a cold cache, a new deploy, or a multi-instance server without a shared cache — it responds with PersistedQueryNotFound and the client must resend the full query.

item.title: Jest: You are trying to import a file after the Jest environment has been torn down
item.description: Asynchronous work outlived the test that started it. When Jest tears down the environment, a still-pending promise, timer or open handle tries to touch module state that no longer exists.

item.title: Kafka: UNKNOWN_TOPIC_OR_PARTITION
item.description: The client asked for a topic the broker does not know about. Either the topic genuinely does not exist, auto-creation is disabled, the client is pointed at the wrong cluster, or the ACLs hide it from this principal.

item.title: kubectl: The connection to the server localhost:8080 was refused
item.description: kubectl found no kubeconfig at all, so it fell back to its built-in default of localhost:8080. This is a client configuration problem, not a cluster outage.

item.title: Kubernetes: 0/N nodes are available — node(s) had untolerated taint
item.description: The scheduler found no node willing to accept the pod because every candidate carries a taint the pod does not tolerate. Control-plane nodes, GPU pools and nodes under pressure are all tainted by default.

item.title: Kubernetes: admission webhook denied the request
item.description: A validating or mutating admission webhook rejected the object. This is policy enforcement — Kyverno, Gatekeeper, cert-manager, an Ingress controller or a service mesh — not an API server fault.

item.title: Kubernetes: Deployment exceeded its progress deadline
item.description: A rollout did not reach the required number of available replicas within progressDeadlineSeconds (600 by default). The Deployment is reporting that the new pods never became ready — the underlying failure is on the pods.

item.title: Kubernetes: Failed to create pod sandbox
item.description: The container runtime could not set up the pod's network namespace. This is a CNI-level failure: the plugin is missing or crashed, the node has exhausted its pod IP range, or the runtime cannot pull the pause image.

item.title: Kubernetes: Init:CrashLoopBackOff
item.description: An init container is failing, so the main containers never start. Init containers run sequentially to completion, and any non-zero exit blocks the whole pod.

item.title: Linux: Read-only file system
item.description: The filesystem was mounted read-only, either intentionally or because the kernel remounted it after detecting I/O errors. The second case means the underlying disk is failing and is urgent.

item.title: LLM: structured output does not match the requested JSON schema
item.description: The model returned prose, a truncated object, or JSON that violates the schema. Usually the response hit the token limit mid-object, or the schema uses features the provider's constrained decoding does not support.

item.title: Loki: entry too far behind / out of order
item.description: Loki rejected log lines whose timestamps are older than the accepted window for that stream. Usually a backfill, a clock-skewed host, or two producers writing to one stream with different clocks.

item.title: macOS: Operation not permitted (Full Disk Access / TCC)
item.description: macOS privacy protection blocked access to a protected location — Desktop, Documents, Downloads, or another application's data — even for a process running as root. The permission is granted to the parent application, so a script run from Terminal needs Terminal to hold it.

item.title: MCP: server connection failed / failed to start
item.description: A Model Context Protocol client could not start or speak to a server. For stdio servers the command is usually wrong or not on PATH; for HTTP servers it is a URL, TLS or auth problem. Anything the server writes to stdout that is not JSON-RPC corrupts the stream.

item.title: Microsoft Entra ID: AADSTS50011 — redirect URI mismatch
item.description: The redirect_uri sent in the authorisation request is not registered on the app registration. Entra requires an exact match including scheme, host, port, path and case, and the platform type must match too.

item.title: MongoDB: Server selection timed out
item.description: The driver could not find a suitable server within serverSelectionTimeoutMS. With Atlas this is nearly always IP access list or DNS/SRV resolution rather than the database being down.

item.title: MySQL: Incorrect string value (utf8mb4 / emoji)
item.description: A four-byte UTF-8 character — most often an emoji — was inserted into a column using MySQL's legacy three-byte 'utf8' (utf8mb3) charset. The value cannot be represented, so the insert fails.

item.title: Next.js: Dynamic server usage — route couldn't be rendered statically
item.description: A route Next.js wanted to prerender at build time used a request-scoped API such as cookies(), headers() or searchParams. Those values do not exist during a static build.
